hooks.note: A UIDocumentPickerViewController shown in a .sheet dismisses the sheet when a document is picked or the picker is cancelled. rememberLauncher dismisses the enclosing Sheet after the result, instead of leaving an empty sheet behind.

UIDocumentPickerViewController(asCopy: true) hands over a file URL of a copy in the temporary Inbox, named after the picked file. A content URI string is not a path, so File(url) in the alert image and sound onUrl (alertMediaStorage.add) and in addLutCube (imageStorage.write) found nothing. copy() copies the document to <cacheDir>/Inbox/<display name> off the main thread and passes its path on the main thread.
The type is a UTType (.gif, .audio, .item) translated to its name, not a MIME type, so the Android picker showed no documents. contentTypes maps it to image/gif, audio/* and */*.
See HDP.2.

See HDP.2. onUrl names the video after the copy (videoName = last path component) and moves it to Documents/Alerts/Videos/<alert id>.<extension> with alertMediaStorage.videos.add, as the Swift VideoView does.
See HDP.1.
See HDP.2. onUrl sets modelName to the picked file name and moves the copy to Documents/PNGTuber/<widget id>.
See HDP.1.
See HDP.2. onUrl checks the path extension of the copy for zip, unzips a Live2D model from the copy, or moves a VRM file to Documents/VTuber/<widget id>.
See HDP.2. importSettingsFromFile reads File(url).
moblinSettingsFileType is the exported UTType identifier com.eerimoq.moblin.settings, which conforms to public.data. No Android provider reports it as a MIME type, so the picker showed nothing.
See HDP.1.

Swift stores url.bookmarkData() of the picked folder and keeps the old value when that fails. Bookmark.data takes a persistable read and write grant on the picked tree, so it resolves after a restart, and returns the tree URI as the bookmark.

URL(resolvingBookmarkData:) of the recording folder. The translation always returned nil, so a recording with a selected folder never started. Bookmark.resolve is nil when the grant is gone or the disk is not connected.
recordingPath.appending(component: name()) inside a document tree is a BookmarkedFile, whose exists() and length() ask the provider.
URL(resolvingBookmarkData:)?.path(): the folder path shown in the recording settings, or nil (Disk not connected?).
The recorder writes to the URL. For a file in a document tree Bookmark.url creates the document and returns its content URI; for any other file it is the path, as before.
See HDP.17.

hooks.old: val size = if (url != null) sizeFormatter.string(fromByteCount = File(url.toString()).length()) else "-"
hooks.new: val size = if (url != null) sizeFormatter.string(fromByteCount = url.length()) else "-"
hooks.note: url.fileSize: File.length() of the recording itself, which a BookmarkedFile asks the provider for.

FileHandle(forWritingAtPath:) on the recording URL. A recording in a selected folder is a content URI, which openOutput opens through the provider (truncated, like Data().write(to:)); any other URL is the file, as before.

hooks.old: appendMedia(model = model, player = player, url = videoItem.toString())
hooks.new: com.moblin.android.platform.DocumentPicker.loadMovie(videoItem) { url -> if (url != null) appendMedia(model = model, player = player, url = url) }
hooks.note: loadTransferable(type: Video.self) copies the picked movie into the temporary directory under its file name, and appendMedia moves that copy to Documents/Medias/<id>.mp4. File(content URI) did not exist, so the playlist got a file that was never stored. loadMovie copies off the main thread and calls back on it, also after the view is gone, like the Swift completion. This parent effect only runs while the parent is composed; the picker and its effect live in the destination, see HDP.29 and HDP.30.
loadTransferable(type: Data.self) fails with an error instead of throwing. Reading on the main thread in the LaunchedEffect crashed the app when the provider threw.
Swift reloads the image widget's effect after storing the picked image, so the new image shows in the scene at once.
FileManager.removeItem removes a directory with its contents. A Live2D VTuber model is a directory, so picking another model for the same widget failed to replace it.
FileManager.moveItem also moves a directory across volumes. copyTo copies only an empty directory.
See HDP.26.

Swift presents the video picker from the Select video button inside the NavigationLink destination. The translation registered the launcher in VideoView, which leaves composition when the destination is shown, so launch() threw on an unregistered launcher. This launcher lives in the destination and shadows the other one.

.photosPicker(isPresented:selection:matching:) is on the Add button inside the NavigationLink destination. The translation put the picker and its effects in MediaPlayerSettingsView, which leaves composition when the destination is shown, so Add did nothing.

hooks.new: LaunchedEffect(selectedVideoItem.value) { selectedVideoItem.value?.let { videoItem -> com.moblin.android.platform.DocumentPicker.loadMovie(videoItem) { url -> if (url != null) appendMedia(model = model, player = player, url = url); selectedVideoItem.value = null } } }
hooks.note: .onChange(of: selectedVideoItem) in the destination, see HDP.29 and HDP.21. loadMovie takes a completion like loadTransferable, so leaving the view while a large video is copied still adds it and moves the copy out of the temporary directory.

FileManager.removeItem removes a directory with its contents. A Live2D VTuber model is a directory, so File.delete() failed and the unused model stayed on disk after its widget was deleted. A missing file still fails like removeItem does.

loadTransferable(type: Data.self) reports a failure instead of throwing. openInputStream and readBytes throw for a photo the picker cannot deliver (a cloud item while offline, a revoked grant), and in the activity result callback that crashed the app. readInput reads the whole photo and returns null on failure.
See HDP.32.
